metadata.title: Generative Adversarial Nets (Goodfellow et al., 2014)
metadata.framework: Adversarial training of generative and discriminative neural networks
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on arXiv:1406.2661 PDF text.

nodes.name: Generator network
nodes.statement: A differentiable function $G(z; \theta_g)$ represented by a multilayer perceptron with parameters $\theta_g$, mapping samples $z$ from a prior noise distribution $p_z(z)$ (e.g., uniform or Gaussian) to data space, implicitly defining a distribution $p_g$ over data $\mathbf{x}$.

nodes.name: Discriminator network
nodes.statement: A multilayer perceptron $D(\mathbf{x}; \theta_d)$ outputting a scalar probability that $\mathbf{x}$ came from the real data distribution $p_{\mathrm{data}}$ rather than the generator distribution $p_g$.

nodes.name: Adversarial minimax objective
nodes.statement: The generator $G$ and discriminator $D$ play a two-player minimax game with value function: $\min_G \max_D V(D, G) = \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{x} \sim p_{\mathrm{data}}}[\log D(\mathbf{x})] + \mathbb{E}_{z \sim p_z}[\log(1 - D(G(z)))]$.

nodes.name: Non-saturating generator loss
nodes.statement: In practice, rather than training $G$ to minimize $\log(1 - D(G(z)))$ (which saturates early), $G$ is trained to maximize $\log D(G(z))$. This provides stronger gradients early in training and has the same fixed point.

nodes.name: Optimal discriminator
nodes.statement: For fixed $G$, the optimal discriminator is $D^*_G(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{p_{\mathrm{data}}(\mathbf{x})}{p_{\mathrm{data}}(\mathbf{x}) + p_g(\mathbf{x})}$.

nodes.name: Optimal discriminator characterization
nodes.statement: For any fixed generator $G$, the optimal discriminator $D$ is $D^*_G(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{p_{\mathrm{data}}(\mathbf{x})}{p_{\mathrm{data}}(\mathbf{x}) + p_g(\mathbf{x})}$.

nodes.name: Global optimum of the minimax game
nodes.statement: The global minimum of the virtual training criterion $C(G) = \max_D V(G, D)$ is achieved if and only if $p_g = p_{\mathrm{data}}$. At that point, $C(G) = -\log 4$, and the optimal discriminator is $D^*(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{1}{2}$ everywhere.

nodes.name: Convergence of Algorithm 1
nodes.statement: If $G$ and $D$ have enough capacity, and at each step of Algorithm 1 the discriminator is allowed to reach its optimum given $G$, and $p_g$ is updated to improve $\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{x} \sim p_{\mathrm{data}}}[\log D^*_G(\mathbf{x})] + \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{x} \sim p_g}[\log(1 - D^*_G(\mathbf{x}))]$, then $p_g$ converges to $p_{\mathrm{data}}$.

nodes.name: Proof of global optimum via JSD
nodes.statement: Substituting $D^*_G$ into $V(G, D^*_G)$ yields $C(G) = -\log 4 + 2 \cdot \mathrm{JSD}(p_{\mathrm{data}} \| p_g)$ where $\mathrm{JSD}$ is the Jensen-Shannon divergence. Since $\mathrm{JSD} \geq 0$ with equality iff $p_{\mathrm{data}} = p_g$, the minimum is $-\log 4$ achieved uniquely at $p_g = p_{\mathrm{data}}$.

nodes.name: Minibatch SGD training of GANs
nodes.statement: For each training iteration: (1) For $k$ steps, sample minibatch of $m$ noise samples $\{z^{(1)}, \ldots, z^{(m)}\}$ and $m$ data examples $\{\mathbf{x}^{(1)}, \ldots, \mathbf{x}^{(m)}\}$, update discriminator by ascending $\nabla_{\theta_d} \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^{m} [\log D(\mathbf{x}^{(i)}) + \log(1 - D(G(z^{(i)})))]$. (2) Sample $m$ noise samples, update generator by descending $\nabla_{\theta_g} \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^{m} \log(1 - D(G(z^{(i)})))$.

nodes.name: Connection to density ratio estimation and NCE
nodes.statement: The GAN discriminator estimates the density ratio $p_{\mathrm{data}}(\mathbf{x})/p_g(\mathbf{x})$, connecting GANs to noise-contrastive estimation (NCE). Unlike NCE, the GAN discriminator is adaptively trained (the noise distribution $p_g$ changes), avoiding the slowdown of NCE with a fixed noise distribution.

nodes.name: No Markov chains needed
nodes.statement: Unlike Boltzmann machines, DBMs, and GSNs, GANs generate samples via a single forward pass through the generator network with no Markov chain mixing required, avoiding mode mixing issues.
